items.title: Greek Social Enterprise Enaleia Makes New York Debut at Climate Week 2026
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK – Greek social enterprise Enaleia, which works to reduce marine plastic pollution and promote sustainable fishing practices, made its New York debut this month at Climate Week NYC. Held September 21-28, Climate Week NYC brings together business leaders, policymakers, environmental organizations, and others for hundreds of events across New York focused on climate action and solutions. Representing Enaleia was Partnerships and Impact Coordinator Fani Sakellariou, who was also visiting New York for the first time. Speaking with The National Herald, Sakellariou reflected on the experience of representing the organization internationally and the opportunities her work has given her to see environmental initiatives and policymaking firsthand. “I’m extremely grateful to the whole team for sending me, and I’ve been very fortunate to have traveled a lot this year for work,” Sakellariou told TNH.

The post Greek Social Enterprise Enaleia Makes New York Debut at Climate Week 2026 appeared first on The National

The official’s comments came after Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran had presented the United States with a “concrete” seven-day plan and that the choice now rested with Washington.

items.title: Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days
items.summary_raw:
Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days

Araghchi met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital energy shipping channel. 

"Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days," Araghchi said at the UN Friday.

"The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure.

"I can tell you if there is seriousness in the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared."

items.title: The Words of Climate, the Climate of Words: How We Talk about a Changing World
items.summary_raw:
Climate change is not purely an environmental or scientific issue. It is also a social, political and — less obviously — linguistic one. Science explains what is happening through indicators and figures and produces ominous of the Earth’s future. Yet society, politics and language largely determine how we perceive reality and, ultimately, how we choose to respond to it. And this may be one of the most critical challenges of our time. Language does not simply describe reality; it also shapes it. The shift from “climate change” to “climate crisis” or “climate collapse” is not merely a matter of vocabulary. Such choices appeal to the emotions of readers and listeners, foster fear, create a sense of urgency and make the need for action more pressing. Language thus becomes a lens through which reality is interpreted, influencing the way we understand the problem. This is why Linguistics[1] examines how the media and social networks talk about climate change through particular linguistic choices.

items.title: METLEN and Dolomiti Energia Inaugurate the Erchie BESS in Apulia
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - METLEN and Dolomiti Energia have inaugurated the new 25 MW/75 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Erchie, Apulia. Its commissioning marks the next milestone for a project first presented earlier this year, when the two companies signed a seven-year physical tolling agreement. Among the first arrangements of its kind in the Italian storage market, the agreement introduces an advanced commercial model that combines the long-term use of the infrastructure with the provision of critical flexibility to the electricity grid. Developed and delivered entirely by METLEN, the project supports the further integration of renewable energy sources and contributes to strengthening the stability of Italy’s electricity system.

The post METLEN and Dolomiti Energia Inaugurate the Erchie BESS in Apulia appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: ‘We don’t have time for more promises’: the Croatian town that took on an illegal waste dump
items.summary_raw:
After years of illegal mass flytipping in Gospić, fed-up residents decided to take matters into their own hands

“Gospić is our home,” Željka Šikić shouted to a crowd of 40,000 people outside the Croatian parliament earlier this month. The slogan is the name of a campaign she helped to set up to protest against the illegal dumping of waste in Gospić, a town in the mountainous Lika region of central Croatia.

Between 2022 and 2024, waste was illegally abandoned at several sites in the town. At one of the biggest, just 50 metres from Šikić’s home, an estimated 35,000 tonnes of waste, some of it hazardous, was dumped and buried.

items.title: Trump Administration Asks the Supreme Court to Allow Quick Third-Country Deportations to Continue
items.summary_raw:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's administration asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to again clear the way for continued quick deportations of immigrants to third countries where they have no ties. The government asked for an immediate halt to lower court orders finding that people must have the chance to object before the U.S. government deports them to countries other than their homelands. The justices allowed the deportation flights to continue when the case came before them last year. Since then, an appeals court has upheld a Boston-based judge’s final ruling that migrants must have a meaningful chance to argue a third-country deportation would put them in danger of persecution or torture. The order doesn't completely prohibit deportations to third countries, but it adds new requirements. The Trump administration says that creates unworkable delays and has already led to the cancellation of a flight carrying 70 people with criminal convictions to three different countries.

They say that the weather pattern, which occurs roughly every two to seven years, may be the strongest in at least a millennium. With its peak yet to come, the temperature rise in the Pacific Ocean has already surpassed the previous high.

The consequence will be huge amounts of heat in an atmosphere already experiencing frighteningly higher temperatures due to the human-caused climate crisis. items.title: Twenty years after An Inconvenient Truth, Al Gore still believes in the climate fight: ‘We are going to win this’
items.summary_raw:
Former US vice-president still has optimism for climate advocacy two decades after groundbreaking documentary

Two decades after the release of his groundbreaking documentary An Inconvenient Truth, Al Gore has admitted he was surprised by the ferocious, ongoing backlash from the fossil fuel industry and its political allies. But the former US vice-president insists he still has optimism the world will confront the climate crisis.

At a New York event to mark the 20th anniversary of the release of the film and his subsequent climate advocacy work, Gore, now 78, joked: “I always say if it hadn’t been for me, we might have a big problem right now” when asked about the progress made over the past two decades.

items.title: Turkey to hand over military base to Iraq
items.summary_raw:
Turkey to hand over military base to Iraq

Turkey will hand over control of its Bashiqa base in northern Iraq to Baghdad, the Turkish presidency announced Wednesday in a joint statement with its neighbour.

"In light of progress achieved by these security measures implemented by Iraq, Turkish forces will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zilkan base to the Federal Government of Iraq in accordance with the agreed mechanism and timetable," a joint statement said.

The announcement followed a meeting Wednesday between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City.

Reporting by AFP

items.title: Asylum Recognition Rate Falls to 37% in 2026
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - The asylum recognition rate stood at 37% during the first eight months of 2026, compared with 72% in 2024 and 58% in 2025, according to sources from the Ministry of Migration and Asylum. The same sources noted that even nationalities with a refugee profile, which in the past had asylum recognition rates of nearly 100%, such as citizens of Afghanistan and Sudan, are now recording recognition rates below 70%. According to the sources, this development is attributed to the immediate rejection of applications on administrative grounds, the application of individualized criteria, and the consideration of the safe third countries through which applicants have passed. According to the same sources, the goal is to further reduce the recognition rate so that asylum is granted only to those who are genuinely entitled to international protection.

The post Asylum Recognition Rate Falls to 37% in 2026 appeared first on The National Herald.

“The EU remains a reliable partner for a peaceful, stable and inclusive transition in Syria, free from harmful foreign interference,” von der Leyen said in a post on X, adding that the EU is working towards Syria’s reconstruction and for the safe, voluntary return of refugees.

“As next steps, we aim to mobilise more investment and upgrade our partnership,” she added.

items.summary_raw:
Libya’s al-Menfi praises Palestinian 'steadfastness' in the face of 'oppression'

Mohamed al-Menfi, head of the Tripoli-based Libyan Presidential Council, said that the 81st session of the United Nation's General Assembly takes place as the world goes through a “profound transformation” in the “balance of power” and the “ethics” surrounding its use.

In remarks delivered at the UN headquarters in New York on Wednesday, he said a major challenge facing the international community is how to build an international order “in which the rule of law is an equal right, not a privilege of the most powerful”.

items.title: ⚡️ ▪️ Despite the Turkish state's open-door policy with the pillars of the Lebanese state, Turkish officials have not yet succeeded in forging an actual relationship with Dar al-Fa…
items.summary_raw: ⚡️ ▪️ Despite the Turkish state's open-door policy with the pillars of the Lebanese state, Turkish officials have not yet succeeded in forging an actual relationship with Dar al-Fatwa, given the lack of enthusiasm from the Grand Mufti of the Republic, Sheikh Abdul Latif Darian, for this matter. Observers attribute this, most likely, to his keenness not to provoke Saudi Arabia. Al-Akhbar learned that Dar al-Fatwa recently refrained from giving an appointment to a Turkish diplomatic delegation concerned with relief affairs, which wished to meet Darian. The delegation had visited a number of political and spiritual authorities, foremost among them Maronite Patriarch Bechara al-Rai, knowing that its purpose for the visit was primarily related to relief files, rather than political ones. It does not seem that Darian's decision to keep the doors of Dar al-Fatwa closed to Ankara is recent. The Grand Mufti of the Republic visits Turkey periodically, as he owns a house there, but he has never visited any of the Turkish political authorities, nor have the Turkish authorities ever prepared official reception ceremonies for him.

items.summary_raw:
New report predicts a heavy toll from Nigeria to the US – and comes on top of existing impacts of the climate crisis

More than 450,000 people are projected to die from the additional heat brought by the super El Niño in the next six months, according to estimates by climate scientists.

The toll is on top of the early deaths resulting from temperatures already driven up by the climate crisis. It will strike across the globe, from Indonesia to India, and Nigeria to the US. Many further deaths are expected from the droughts, wildfires and flooding that El Niños bring.

items.title: Report: Hormuz traffic on Tuesday below 10-day average
items.summary_raw:
Report: Hormuz traffic on Tuesday below 10-day average

Three commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from four a day earlier and below the 10-day moving average of about 15, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday.

The figures may change as some ships typically switch off their transponders during the voyage.
All three vessels, including one Panamax tanker, were exiting the strait, the data from shiptracker Kpler showed at 0200 GMT.

One ballast liquefied natural gas tanker, Al Mafyar, however reappeared inside the strait on Tuesday, after being last seen outside of the waterway on September 19, according to both Kpler and LSEG data.

The Strait of Hormuz carried a fifth of the world's oil and gas before the US-Iran conflict.

items.title: Rubio says US open to meeting Iranian officials at UN
items.summary_raw:
Rubio says US open to meeting Iranian officials at UN

Washington is open to the idea of meeting Iranian officials at the United Nations, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said, adding that no meeting has been scheduled. 

“We’re open to that. I don’t think anything is scheduled at this point,” Rubio said in an interview with NBC News’ Today show, adding that such a meeting would be useful if it could lead to a positive outcome.

According to Rubio, preventing Iran from getting a nuclear weapon remained the primary US goal. 

“And that is the fact that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon. They just simply can’t,” he said. 

His comments come as diplomatic efforts continue amid soaring tensions between Washington and Tehran.

items.summary_raw:
The ‘Godzilla-level’ phenomenon is supercharging the climate crisis and will heavily impact communities across the world

The “jaw-dropping” El Niño currently heating up the planet has burst through the highest temperature ever recorded for the phenomenon, several months ahead of its expected peak.

The latest data shows the temperature rise at the heart of El Niño in the Pacific ocean has now reached 3.05C. That is higher than the 3.02C set in late November 2015, the previous high set in the 150 years of modern records. This temperature is measured against the average of 1991-2020.

items.title: Gerapetritis in Toronto: Power, AI and New Alliances in a Changing Geopolitical Era
items.summary_raw:
TORONTO. Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis said the world is entering a new geopolitical era in which power is carrying increasing weight compared with principles and international rules, during an address at the University of Toronto. Speaking to students and members of the academic community, the Foreign Minister described an international environment in which armed conflicts, energy and food insecurity, water scarcity and technological change interact, creating what he called an “explosive mix.” He placed particular emphasis on what he described as the erosion of international law and multilateralism, arguing that the postwar security architecture is facing increasing pressure. According to the Minister, contemporary crises are no longer geographically contained. Wars affect international energy and food markets, while regional tensions produce broader political, economic and social consequences. Referring to water scarcity, he warned that the distribution of water resources could become one of the most serious sources of conflict for future generations.

items.title: US environment agency let Bayer pick regulations for destructive weedkiller, documents show
items.summary_raw:
Environmental Protection Agency asked firm to choose rules it wanted for dicamba, then put the choices in a proposed federal rule

The EPA allowed pesticide giant Bayer to pick from a menu of regulation options for the controversial and destructive weedkiller dicamba, newly released internal agency documents show.

The documents provide an unusually clear look into the process of developing pesticide regulations, which is typically done out of public view. It shows in detail how the EPA asked Bayer which regulations it wanted, received a response from Bayer, then put Bayer’s choices into a proposed federal rule.

items.title: 来自中国电网的超级气候污染物正在炙烤地球
items.summary_raw: Read this article in English. 中国的电网有一个肮脏的秘密：尽管它在可再生能源发展引领全球，它也是地球上最强效温室气体的最大排放源。 六氟化硫（SF6）是一种合成化学物质，在高压设备中作为电气绝缘介质发挥着至关重要的角色。这种气体无色无味、无毒、且不可燃。但它也是气候杀手，按等质量计算，其使地球变暖的效力是二氧化碳的24,300倍。一旦释放，六氟化硫会在大气中存留1,000年。 排放主要来自电力行业。该行业中将这种气体用于断路器和其他高压设备中，以防止电弧放电。六氟化硫几乎无法被破坏，是任何现代电网的关键安全屏障，确保电力只在需要时流向所需之处。然而，当中国的电气设备达到使用寿命终点时，其中大部分的气体很可能被排放到大气中。 早在2014年，中国政府研究员就警告称，六氟化硫“对全球环境构成重大潜在威胁”。然而，这种气候污染物的排放在中国仍是未受监管的。 中国生态环境部最近表示，中国电力企业当前回收—或有能力回收—其废弃六氟化硫气体的90%。然而，Inside Climate News估算，实际回收率要低得多，仅为30%。这些企业只需付出很低的成本，就能将回收率提高到约90%，从而大幅减少温室气体排放。 该分析参考了数百页的政府文件、中国主要电力企业的年度报告、经同行评审的研究，以及对数十位学者和政策专家的采访。根据这项评估，Inside Climate News估算，中国国有的输配电企业每年可将从电气设备中回收的六氟化硫量增加约1,400吨。这样做有望减少中国所有行業该污染物的总排放量近三分之一，预计每年成本约为600万美元，这仅占中国每年投资电网约700亿美元的一小部分。 如果把这种气体排放到大气，而不是将其回收，那简直就是一场三级火警，美国环境保护署前含氟温室气体排放分析师黛博拉·奥廷格在谈到Inside Climate News的评估时说道。“这是一项非常显而易见且可以立即实施的措施。” 生态环境部、位于华盛顿的中国驻美国大使馆，以及国家电网有限公司和中国南方电网有限责任公司，均拒绝就调查结果发表评论。国家电网和南方电网是两家国有电力企业，共同为几乎全国供电。 据2024年发表于《自然-通讯》期刊的一项研究，全球超过一半的六氟化硫排放量来自中国。尽管其他地区的该气体排放量有所减少，中国的排放量在2011年至2021年间几乎加倍，预计还将继续攀升。在2021年，目前有数据可查的最近年份，中国排放了5,100吨六氟化硫。这污染量相当于2,900万辆燃油汽车的年度温室气体排放量。 去年，全球大气中六氟化硫浓度出现了自1998年有记录以来最大的年度增幅，显示中国的排放量仍在上升。 “就全球变暖潜能和大气寿命而言，这几乎是最糟糕的温室气体。” 布里斯托大学大气化学教授、《自然-通讯》研究的共同作者马修·里格比说。“一旦进入大

items.title: Turkish foreign minister says new proposals sent to US, Iran to end war
items.summary_raw:
Turkish foreign minister says new proposals sent to US, Iran to end war

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said that Turkey and other countries have proposed new conditions to the US and Iran to end the war.

Fidan told Turkish television channel NTV:  “Turkey and other countries are presenting proposals and are making every effort to bring the negotiations between the United States and Iran to a conclusion.” 

“But there is a strong distrust between the parties. They had previously reached an agreement in Pakistan, but then problems arose in its implementation. Now both sides are clearly trying to advance this process in a way that will secure their interests.”

items.summary_raw: Visioner BIG | 🇮🇷🇺🇸🇮🇱‼️‼️ Iran is openly signaling that future U.S. and Israeli actions could push Tehran toward withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, although Iranian officials insist that no such decision has been made.  Speaking to Al Jazeera, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said any potential withdrawal from the NPT would depend on Washington’s next moves. He maintained that Iran remains committed to Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei’s religious decree prohibiting the development of nuclear weapons and said Tehran’s nuclear doctrine has not changed, while adding, “We do not know what will happen in the future.”  An Iranian withdrawal from the NPT would represent a major escalation in the nuclear confrontation, weakening the international framework governing Tehran’s nuclear activities and adding another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile conflict. For now, Rezaei’s remarks amount to a warning rather than a declared policy change, with Tehran explicitly tying its future position to what the United States and Israel do next. items.title: Turkey says it will look into Saudi military needs as part of defence pact
items.summary_raw:
Turkey says it will look into Saudi military needs as part of defence pact

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday that Saudi Arabia may have some military needs due to the ongoing attacks by Yemen's Houthis and that Turkey would look into them as part of a trilateral defence pact signed with Pakistan.

Speaking on broadcaster NTV, Fidan said it was unacceptable for Saudi Arabia to be made a part of the US-Iran war, as it had no desire to join the conflict, and added without elaborating, that proposals have been conveyed to all sides to end the fighting.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Joint Defence Agreement in August in Mecca, under which an attack on one member would be treated as an attack on all.

items.summary_raw: ⚡️ MBDA Stratus Missile This program is being pursued by a European consortium comprising France, Italy, and the United Kingdom to produce two different missiles that will replace all land-attack and anti-ship missiles currently in service with these countries, including Harpoon, Exocet, and Storm Shadow. The first missile, known as Stratus-LO, is a subsonic cruise missile with a currently confidential range, though it is expected to be equal to or greater than the 1000-kilometer range of the American AGM-158B JASSM-ER, and is designed for attacking targets deep within enemy territory. The second missile, known as Stratus-RS, is a supersonic anti-ship missile with a likely shorter range of approximately 600-800 kilometers, which will have a flight and performance profile similar to the Russian P-800 Oniks M or the Chinese YJ-12, albeit with much more advanced technology. These missiles are intended for use in two versions: air-launched from Rafale, Typhoon, and F-35 fighter jets, and vertical-launched from Sylver A70 launchers used on the warships of these three countries.
